title: Lesson 36: Testing Agents: Unit Tests for Tools, Integration Tests, and Regression Evals
description: Replacing the vibe check with three layers: unit tests over the deterministic machinery, integration tests across the full loop against controlled tool side effects, and regression evals scoring real output against a frozen golden set.

questions.question: Per the lesson "Testing Agents: Unit Tests for Tools, Integration Tests, and Regression Evals", what is the one idea to carry out?
options: Test the properties of outputs rather than exact outputs, test the deterministic layers as ordinary software, and score the fuzzy end with an evaluator kept honest by a frozen baseline
Assert exact output strings and fail the build whenever they change
Skip automated testing because agent output is stochastic
Rely on manual review of every run before release
questions.explanation: The lesson says the model is a moving target, so you wrap it in checks you can pin down and add an evaluator layer for the fuzzy end, turning is it ready to ship into a number with a threshold.

questions.question: How does the lesson define an integration test for an agent?
options: A test that stubs the model and asserts on a prompt string
A test that runs the whole agent loop against controlled tool side effects, asserting the sequence and outcome, such as the right tool called with the right arguments in the right order
A test that scores real output with an LLM judge against a golden set
A test that measures cost per request under load
questions.explanation: The lesson defines integration tests as running the whole loop with mocked tools that return fixed data, so the assertion is on tool selection, argument formation, ordering, and that nothing destructive happened.

questions.question: The lesson says teams sink their testing effort by leading with the expensive layer. What structure does it recommend instead?
options: Run LLM-as-judge evaluations on every commit
Replace unit tests with live production experiments
A costed pyramid: cheap deterministic assertions on every pull request, model-based evaluation nightly or before release, and live experiments only after the lower layers pass
Test only in production and roll back on failure
questions.explanation: The lesson describes the pyramid explicitly, warning that wiring up expensive eval judges on every commit leads teams to quietly stop running them.
